entries.appliesTo: persons who use, publish, distribute, or cause the publication of content containing an individual's personal identity

dutySources.consent-workflow: § 45-3-3(1)(a) — 'each individual has the exclusive right to consent to the use of the individual's personal identity'; § 45-3-3(2)(a)(ii) — 'consent has not been obtained from the individual'

sources.consentRequired: § 45-3-3(1)(a) — 'each individual has the exclusive right to consent to the use of the individual's personal identity'
sources.coveredSubjects: § 45-3-2(6) — '"Individual" means a natural person, living or dead.'
sources.postmortemYears: § 45-3-3(1)(b)(iii) — 'does not expire until 70 years after the death of the individual'
sources.enforcer: § 45-3-4(1) — 'may bring an action against a person who caused the publication of the advertisement or content'; § 45-3-5(1) — 'may bring an action against a person who published the advertisement or content'

flags: Defamation provisions fit no family: § 45-2-3.5 makes AI/digital creation no defense to libel or slander ('It is not a defense to a claim of libel or slander that the communication was created through generative artificial intelligence'); § 45-2-14 requires pre-suit written notice for actions based on digitally created content and limits recovery to actual damages 'if the person who published or caused the publication of the digitally created content removes the content within 10 days' after notice

Tool-trafficking prohibition fits no duty key: § 45-3-3(2)(c) — abuse includes when a person 'knowingly distributes, sells, or licenses any technology, software, or tool whose intended primary purpose is the unauthorized creation or modification of content that includes an individual's personal identity'

Safe-harbor disclosure not coded as disclosure-ui because it is an optional defense, not a mandate: § 45-3-3(5) — no abuse under (2)(b) if distribution 'is accompanied by a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the content is a simulation or artificial recreation of the individual'
Retroactive postmortem right: § 45-3-3(1)(b)(v) — for an individual who died before May 6, 2026, the right 'applies retroactively for up to 70 years before May 6, 2026'
No penaltyMax: remedies are uncapped civil relief — § 45-3-4(2) 'injunctive relief, damages alleged and proved, exemplary damages, and reasonable attorney fees and costs'
Interactive computer services exempt under both chapters: § 45-2-14(5) and § 45-3-7(3) (47 U.S.C. 230)
Criminal enforcement only by cross-reference, not coded: § 45-3-3(3) — 'Nothing in this chapter prohibits prosecution of abuse of personal identity under Section 76-12-304'
